In this model, switching is based on social interaction and herding rather than profitability considerations. Alfarano et al. (2005) show that in this model the tail behavior of the distributions of returns is a function of the herding tendency of agents.
is also in line with Franke and Westerhoff (2012, 2016) who estimate various HAMs and show that herding behavior plays a key role in matching the stylized facts.

the noise traders play an important role in generating insignificant ACs on the returns, while the significantly decayed AC patterns of the absolute returns and squared returns are more influenced by the fundamental noise.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: In the Kirman / Alfarano social-interaction lineage, fat tails and volatility clustering are not assumed but emerge endogenously from herding among heterogeneous agents; the tail heaviness becomes a function of the herding tendency rather than of exogenous shocks.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Emergent Fat Tails and Volatility Clustering From Herding
